title: An exact KP line soliton from a traveling-wave reduction
status: Developed classical result with a scoped worked example
summary: The source proposed a symbolic tanh solver. A complete solution begins by fixing the PDE normalization and deriving the algebraic constraints. The single-soliton family provides an exact benchmark for a symbolic solver and a numerical residual.
definitions: Use (u_t+6uu_x+u_xxx)_x+3s u_yy=0 with s=+1 or -1.
Let X=x+ell*y-c*t, k>0, and impose decay of U(X), U-prime and U-double-prime at both infinities.

result.name: Exact traveling-wave and tau-function identity
result.statement: u(x,y,t)=2k² sech²(kX) solves KP when c=4k²+3s*ell². It also equals2 partial_x² log(1+exp(2kX)).
result.proof: Substitution gives [-cU-prime+6UU-prime+U-triple-prime]-prime+3s*ell² U-double-prime=0. Integrate twice using the stated decay to obtain U-double-prime+(3s*ell²-c)U+3U²=0. For f=sech²(kX), direct differentiation yields f-double-prime=4k²f-6k²f². Setting U=2k²f therefore gives U-double-prime=4k²U-3U²; the reduced ODE vanishes exactly at the stated speed. Differentiating log(1+exp(2kX)) twice gives k²sech²(kX), proving the tau representation. The tanh form is U=2k²[1-tanh²(kX)], so degree balancing M=2 becomes a verified consequence in this example.

example.calculation: The amplitude is1/2, speed c=4 and profile U(X)=(1/2)sech²(X/2). At X=0, U=1/2 and U-double-prime=-1/4, so U-double-prime- U+3U²=-1/4-1/2+3/4=0. Its line-integrated mass is integral U dX=4k=2.
example.conclusion: All solution parameters and the PDE residual are determined analytically.

limits: A KP solution alone establishes neither a tsunami source model nor accuracy near shorelines, breaking waves or varying bathymetry. Those require additional equations and data.
extension: Extend the symbolic procedure to a two-exponential tau function and derive the interaction coefficient from the bilinear KP identity; verify the one-soliton limit before numerical comparisons.

title: Finite-field Hilbert90 as an exact descent calculation
status: Developed classical result with a scoped worked example
summary: The source requested a concrete Hilbert90 example rather than an unspecified obstruction. A quadratic finite field makes the cocycle, norm and coboundary entirely visible.
definitions: Let F49=F7[a]/(a²-3);3 is not a square in F7.
The nontrivial Galois automorphism is sigma(a)=a^7=-a. A multiplicative1-cocycle for this cyclic group is specified by u with u*sigma(u)=1.

result.name: Explicit finite-field Hilbert90
result.statement: Every norm-one u in F49-star is v/sigma(v). The element u=5-a is obtained from v=1+a.
result.proof: The multiplicative group F49-star is cyclic of order48. Its norm is x maps to x^8, whose image has order6 and whose kernel has order8. The homomorphism v maps to v/sigma(v)=v^(-6) has kernel F7-star of order6, hence image of order8. Every image element has norm1 by cancellation, so image and norm kernel coincide. For the explicit example, (1+a)/(1-a)=(1+a)²/(1-a²)=(4+2a)/5=5+6a=5-a in F7. Its norm is(5-a)(5+a)=25-3=22=1 modulo7. Thus the cocycle is a coboundary with an explicit witness.

example.setup: Represent field elements by pairs(r,s), meaning r+s*a, with multiplication(r,s)(t,v)=(rt+3sv,rv+st) modulo7.
example.calculation: Enumeration gives48 nonzero elements,8 norm-one elements and8 distinct ratios v/sigma(v). The displayed ratio and norm both hold exactly in this pair arithmetic.
example.conclusion: The descent claim is certified by finite algebra, and its witness can be independently replayed.

limits: Hilbert90 eliminates this particular multiplicative cocycle obstruction. It does not solve arbitrary discrete logarithms or identify every arithmetic obstruction with a finite-field cocycle.
extension: Generalize the enumerator to F(q^n), compare the norm kernel with the image of v/sigma(v), and then separate linear-algebra cost from a discrete-logarithm representation of the same elements.

status: Developed classical result with a scoped worked example

title: A Mellin split gives a reproducible central L-value formula
status: Developed classical result with a scoped worked example
summary: The historical approximate-functional-equation outputs disagree even in sign. For a weight-two form, splitting the Mellin integral at the Fricke fixed point gives a rapidly convergent center formula whose normalization can be checked directly.
definitions: Let f(tau)=sum(n>=1)a_n exp(2pi*i*n*tau) be a weight-two cusp form of level N.
Assume f(i/(N*t))=epsilon*N*t²*f(i*t), epsilon=+1 or -1, and |a_n|<=2n. Put c=2pi/sqrt(N).

result.name: Exact central-value series with an explicit tail
result.statement: L(1,f)=(1+epsilon)sum(n>=1)(a_n/n)exp(-c*n). Truncation after M terms has absolute tail at most2|1+epsilon|exp[-c(M+1)]/(1-exp(-c)).
result.proof: The Mellin identity gives L(1,f)=2pi integral(0,infinity)f(i*t)dt. Set A=1/sqrt(N) and substitute t=1/(N*u) in the lower integral. The Fricke identity turns it into epsilon integral(A,infinity)f(i*u)du. Thus the full integral equals(1+epsilon) times the upper integral. Termwise integration is justified by absolute exponential convergence on t>=A and gives the stated series. The coefficient bound yields |a_n/n|<=2, so a geometric series bounds the omitted tail. In particular epsilon=-1 forces the center value to vanish. For an elliptic newform, the bound follows from |a_n|<=d(n)sqrt(n) and the elementary inequality d(n)<=2sqrt(n).

example.setup: For N=11 use f=eta(tau)²eta(11*tau)², whose Fricke sign is epsilon=+1.
example.calculation: The q product q*product(1-q^n)²(1-q^(11n))² yields exact integer coefficients. Twenty terms give approximately0.2538418608559107, with analytic tail below3e-17 under the coefficient bound. The numerical approximation has its own rounding error; the tail formula is independent of quadrature-node choices.
example.conclusion: The local normalization, functional equation and truncation error are exposed rather than hidden in a generic AFE routine.

limits: The theorem assumes genuine modular coefficients and the stated Fricke law. Applying it to arbitrary surrogate traces would not construct a modular L-function.
extension: Implement interval exponential evaluation and retain the exact Fourier coefficients plus the analytic tail to produce a completely rounded central-value enclosure.

title: A calibrated search has a computable multiplicity cost
status: Developed classical result with a scoped worked example
summary: The source moonshine interpretation selected fitted coordinates and reported a significance value. A finite family of tests gives an exact mathematical benchmark for distinguishing one prespecified statistic from a selected maximum.
definitions: Let p1,...,pM be valid null p-values, so Pr(pj<=u)<=u for each j.

result.name: Finite-search familywise control
result.statement: Pr(p_adj<=alpha)<=alpha. If the p-values are independent uniform variables, Pr(min pj<=u)=1-(1-u)^M exactly.
result.proof: The event p_adj<=alpha is contained in the union of events pj<=alpha/M. The union bound gives probability at most sum_j alpha/M=alpha, proving the adjusted test. Under independence, the complementary event pj>u for all j has probability(1-u)^M, giving the exact formula. The theorem concerns the whole specified search family: fitting extra parameters, choosing observables after inspection or retaining only successful seeds enlarges that family or requires a different null calibration. A held-out evaluation can avoid reusing the same observations for both selection and confirmation.

example.calculation: The chance of at least one such small p-value is1-0.999^1000, approximately0.6323. Thus a selected value0.001 does not carry the interpretation of one prespecified test.
example.conclusion: The cost of selection can be computed without asserting any physical mechanism or interpreting fitted couplings as predictions.

title: Compounding distinguishes price growth from purchasing-power decay
status: Developed classical result with a scoped worked example
summary: The source challenged an invented annual rate. The mathematical repair is to state a hypothetical rate transparently and distinguish the two reciprocal quantities before inserting any empirical index.
definitions: Let the annual price multiplier be1+pi>0 and the annual purchasing-power multiplier be1-d>0.

result.name: Exact reciprocal compounding
result.statement: (1-d)=1/(1+pi), so d=pi/(1+pi). After T years the price factor is(1+pi)^T and the purchasing-power factor is(1-d)^T.
result.proof: If one basket costs P0 initially and PT=P0(1+pi)^T later, a fixed nominal amount buys PT/P0 times fewer baskets; its relative purchasing power is P0/PT. Equating the annual reciprocal factor with1-d gives the stated conversion. For variable annual rates pi_t, replace the power by the product of(1+pi_t); averaging rates arithmetically does not in general reproduce that product. The constant equivalent annual rate is exp[T^(-1)sum log(1+pi_t)]-1. These are index identities, not estimates of any country or historical period.

example.setup: Stipulate d=0.033 for T=30; do not treat it as a measured historical rate.
example.calculation: The purchasing-power factor is0.967^30, approximately0.3654, and the reciprocal price factor is about2.7366. The corresponding price inflation rate is0.033/0.967, approximately3.4126 percent, rather than3.3 percent.
